source.title: Grok Bot
source.description: What Bots can do: teamwork, a shared cloud computer, voice, app and MCP connections, and prebuilt marketplace Bots.

source.title: Get started
source.description: Install the app, which plans include it, SSO and Grok account sign-in, and a first task set to repeat.

source.title: Use Cases
source.description: Starter prompts for app-connected tasks, single-job Bots like sales or invoicing, and multi-Bot teams like month-end close.

source.title: How Grok Bot Works
source.description: One request traced end to end: per-Bot vs shared memory, login lookup order, Auto Review, and why Bots aren't isolated.

source.title: Message and collaborate
source.description: Voice and dictation, reviewing drafts, group chats and Bot handoffs, X Chat fixes, shopping and phone calls.

source.title: Files and results
source.description: Attachment size limits, moving files via Drive or email, image and video generation, pages, the Library, Cloud Agent outputs.

source.title: Use the computer and apps
source.description: Connect apps, custom MCP servers or 1Password; fix Google or Microsoft admin blocks; claim a `mail.grokbot.com` address; recover an unreachable computer.

source.title: Create and manage Bots
source.description: Setting a primary Bot, renaming, hiding vs deleting, sharing templates, and viewing, correcting, forgetting or importing what a Bot remembers.

source.title: Skills and routines
source.description: Save, publish or demonstrate skills; trigger routines from Slack, webhooks or email; why one didn't run; rate limits and usage.

source.title: Approvals, security, and privacy
source.description: Answer approval cards and why they expire, write Ask first or Allow automatically rules, allow local-computer commands, and revoke access.

source.title: Vault and secure sign-in
source.description: CSV import, API key and Team Bot secrets, approving every payment, order cards, and why saved values look blank or deleted.

source.title: Team Bots
source.description: Who can change a shared Bot, why lessons need approval, and whose apps and usage apply in shared chats.

source.title: Create and share a Team Bot
source.description: Publish and share it, connect it to Slack or Microsoft Teams, approve its learnings, and share one app account.

source.title: Grok Bot for Mobile
source.description: Cancelling App Store or Google Play subscriptions, Siri shortcuts, and letting Bots use your phone's Calendar, Contacts or Home.

source.title: Use Grok Bot in Microsoft Teams
source.description: Admin approval, linking your Microsoft account, files via OneDrive, and fixing "Waiting on admin approval" or blocked custom apps.

source.title: Add a Bot to Your Meetings
source.description: Join Google Meet, Zoom or Teams calls by link or calendar; mute or remove the Bot; summaries, transcripts and plan availability.

source.title: When Your Bot Takes Initiative
source.description: What the primary Bot does unprompted, like offering tasks or flagging signed-out apps, and how to mute its alerts.

source.title: Tag @bot on X
source.description: Account and region requirements (not UK, EU or Australia), what each @bot reply means, and why @bot stayed silent.

source.title: Grok Bot for teams and enterprises
source.description: Large admin reference: every dashboard control and which are Enterprise only, group overrides, Team Secrets, retention, Action Recording, recommended baseline.

source.title: Deploy Grok Bot to your organization
source.description: Push installers with MDM or `.deb`/`.rpm`, pin a version, why auto-updates can't be turned off, and the Update required screen.

source.title: Configure identity and access
source.description: Fix "User is not assigned to this application" in Okta or Entra ID, and IdP device rules blocking the Bot's computer.

source.title: Set up Okta Verify and FastPass
source.description: Enterprise only: install via the `setup-okta.sh` Team Setup Script, enrol each computer once, and avoid the Ctrl+V passcode crash.

source.title: Connect to private networks
source.description: Reach intranet or VPC services by installing Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel with Team Setup Scripts and Team Secrets.

source.title: Configure TLS-inspecting proxies
source.description: Hosted computer setup failing behind Zscaler or other gateways: the `*.*.cursorvm.com` allowlist and TLS inspection exemptions.

source.title: Manage Grok Bot computers
source.description: Enterprise admins: bulk recreate, terminate or wipe members' computers via dashboard or API, auto-delete inactive ones, and read failed results.

source.title: Grok Bot inference hooks
source.description: Large reference: route model requests and tool calls to your security server for allow/deny verdicts; signing, fail-open/closed modes, frame JSON.

source.title: Grok Bot security
source.description: Network policy modes, blocked sites and connector hosts, credential handling, audit logs and data residency.

source.title: Grok Bot security FAQ
source.description: Quick answers for security reviews: microVM isolation, egress IPs, Zscaler hangs, model restrictions, data residency, certifications.

source.title: Settings and notifications
source.description: Where each option lives, why alerts reach desktop not phone, and routing traffic through your desktop.

source.title: Deep links
source.description: Build `grokbot://` links that prefill a Bot's message from shortcuts or other apps, plus plugin install links.

source.title: Troubleshooting
source.description: Sign-in loops, outages, an unreachable computer (Recover vs Reset), plugin auth failures, sites timing out, and what to send support.

source.title: Frequently asked questions
source.description: Grab-bag answers: Grok app vs Grok Bot, no model picker, SuperGrok linking, usage caps, trials, refunds, account deletion.
